ădoptātīcĭus (not -tītĭus ), a, um, adj. adopto,
I.adopted, received in the place of a child; only in Plaut., Poen. 5, 2, 85: “Demarcho item ipse fuit adoptaticius,” ib. 100 . —Acc. to Festus, it signifies the son of one who is adopted: ex adoptato filio natus, p. 29 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
